question.text: A particle executes simple harmonic motion represented by displacement function as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. If the position and velocity of the particle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>ω</mi><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively, then its amplitude is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> where the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is

solution.text:
x(t)=Asin(ωt+ϕ)

v(t)=Aωcos(ωt+ϕ)

2=Asinϕ ...1

2ω=Aωcosϕ  ...2

From (1) and (2)

tanϕ=1

ϕ=45°

Putting the value of ϕ in equation (1)

2=A12

A=22

x=2
